title: Sort each physical quantity into its dimensional family
instructions: Each card shows a physical quantity. Drop it into the bin whose dimensional formula matches. Use the SI definition (e.g. force = mass × acceleration) to derive the formula if you don't remember it directly.

bins.name: [M L² T⁻²]
bins.description: Energy-like: force × distance, or mass × velocity².

items.name: Force
items.explanation: F = m a → kg · (m/s²) → [M L T⁻²].

items.name: Weight
items.explanation: Weight is a force (mg), so same dimensions as force: [M L T⁻²].

items.name: Tension
items.explanation: Tension is a force in a string; [M L T⁻²].

items.name: Kinetic energy
items.explanation: KE = (1/2) m v² → kg · (m/s)² → [M L² T⁻²].

items.name: Work
items.explanation: W = F · d → [M L T⁻²] × L → [M L² T⁻²].

items.name: Torque
items.explanation: τ = r × F → L × [M L T⁻²] → [M L² T⁻²]. Same dimensions as energy, different physical meaning.

items.name: Linear momentum
items.explanation: p = m v → kg · (m/s) → [M L T⁻¹].

items.name: Impulse
items.explanation: Impulse = F · t = change in momentum → [M L T⁻²] × T → [M L T⁻¹].

items.name: Pressure
items.explanation: P = F / A → [M L T⁻²] / L² → [M L⁻¹ T⁻²].

items.name: Stress
items.explanation: Stress = force / area, same dimensions as pressure.

items.name: Power
items.explanation: Power = energy / time → [M L² T⁻²] / T → [M L² T⁻³].
